chapter: Sarah Vaughan and the Basie band
title: Starting with Sarah Vaughan: the rhythm section and the road
summary: Working with Sarah Vaughan from about 1947 with John Collins in Birdland, no rehearsals, then leaving because of his health.

story.theme_name: Singers and the musicians who accompanied them
story.community_name: Joe Williams: the singer with Basie

blocks.x: So you and John have been friends and musical associates. Have you worked together in between here, a year or so ago, and way back in the beginning?

Oh, we did work together in New York, after we both wound up in New York. This was with Sarah Vaughan, in Birdland. We had a very good rhythm section with her. It was Al McKivven (PHONETIC), Kibbon, John Collins. I played piano, and Joe Jones on drums.
What year was that?
Oh, boy, wait a minute. I really have to -- I was with Sarah -- it had to be in the '50s, I guess.
Uh-huh.
You know, or around that time. I can't pinpoint the year. But after -- I have to think in terms of groups. I know where I was when I became ill, you know, and then when I came back to Sarah.
But you started with Sarah in the late '40s, didn't you?
Yes. Coming out of Cafe Society. This was about '47, 1947. And we just turned out to be a good match.
Yeah, you did some beautiful things together.
Yeah, we were just, naturals, and the funny thing about it, we never rehearsed, we never had a bad
word. We would just go on the stand and play.
No arrangements?

No, we didn't have any arrangements. I didn't start writing -- I started writing, after I left her, writing for her after I left her, when I began to free lance in New York, and I started writing for Joe Williams, Sarah, and Lena, and you know, there was a bunch of them. And I was just the accompanist at that time.
But you did beautiful things with her, behind her. It was a very effective combination, you and Sarah.

Yes. We were just lucky that the chemistry was there. And we knew that we felt comfortable. That's the reason that we never thought about worrying about music. We just didn't worry about it. You know, it was one of those things. And I really enjoyed it. It was so comical that I stayed on the road so long. I enjoyed her singing so much. So I used to tell my wife, I says, 'Baby, you'd better join me,' because I'd go out for eight or nine months on the road. I'd tell my wife, 'Hey, you'd better come on out here now. It's just too long to be apart.'
Uh-huh.
But I wasn't about to leave Sarah. The only thing that got -- that I left Sarah for was my health began to get a little shaky, and the road was getting rough on
me, you know?
Uh-huh.

And I would always -- after I built up, then I would always get a little gunshy, I'd say, "Wait a minute. I'd better take a rest. Take it easy." You know? But I really missed her. We did a nice thing at the union, in the Local 47, on behalf of Erroll Garner.
Yeah, I remember. I was there. It was beautiful.
Yeah. And --
You and Kenny Burrell.
Kenny Burrell, -- let's see, I forget who was playing bass.
I do too. I just remember you and Kenny. And Sarah.
